title: Efficacy and integration of different control methods against Ostrinia nubilalis Hübner (Lepidoptera: Crambidae) and Sesamia nonagrioides Lefebvre (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae) in Çukurova, Turkey
content:
Abstract
Lepidopteran stem borers—the European corn borer, Ostrinia nubilalis Hübner (Lepidoptera: Crambidae), and the Mediterranean corn borer, Sesamia nonagrioides Lefèbvre (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae)—cause substantial yield losses in maize production across the Mediterranean basin, yet reliance on broad-spectrum insecticides, particularly pyrethroids, in this system suppresses natural enemy activity and limits the development of sustainable integrated pest management (IPM) programs. A two-year field study (2012–2013) was conducted in Mersin province, Çukurova, Turkey, to compare the efficacy of four management strategies: integrated management (IM; mating disruption [MD] combined with inundative releases of Trichogramma evanescens Westwood [Hymenoptera: Trichogrammatidae]), biotechnical management (BTM; MD alone), chemical management (CM; three pyrethroid applications), and an untreated control (UC). MD targeting S. nonagrioides reduced egg mass densities by 37%–73% relative to UC across both years. Inundative T. evanescens releases at 10,000 parasitoids per decare (100,000 per hectare) achieved 92%–96% parasitism of O. nubilalis egg masses—providing larval suppression of this pest comparable to that achieved by chemical control—while leaving natural enemy activity intact. CM produced the highest grain yields (717–751 kg/da) but markedly suppressed natural parasitism of both borer species. IM yields (568–649 kg/da) exceeded UC (338–440 kg/da) by 40%–68% and were similar to BTM (552–622 kg/da). These findings demonstrate that combining MD with augmentative T. evanescens releases provides effective, pesticide-free management of both corn borer species simultaneously, offering a viable IPM alternative for Mediterranean maize production.
